overall: Los Angeles is in the very early hours of June 25 (00:20 ET / ~9:20 PM PT on June 24), with the running TMAX so far at just 62.6°F — effectively an overnight minimum. Conditions reflect the classic June marine layer pattern: patchy fog, mostly cloudy overnight, SW winds 0-10 mph, and a dewpoint of 57.2°F indicating significant marine moisture. Temperatures are flat or slightly cooling as expected at this hour, with the true daily warming cycle still hours away.
forecast_obs_notes: NWP models are in tight agreement: ECMWF at 68.3°F, HRRR at 68.6°F, and NBM slightly cooler at 67.0°F — a spread of only ~1.6°F, which is narrow and confidence-building. The NWS official forecast of 69°F is consistent with this consensus. The intraday obs-driven bucket distribution shows a wide, uncertain spread peaking in the 74-79°F range, but this should be discounted heavily given we are at the very start of the observational window with almost no daytime heating data yet; the NWP consensus is far more informative at this stage.
max_temp_prediction: Today's TMAX for Los Angeles is most likely to land near 68°F, squarely in the ECMWF/HRRR consensus zone and just slightly below the NWS official 69°F. The persistent marine layer and patchy fog through mid-morning will limit early warming, and partly sunny skies in the afternoon should allow modest heating but not enough to break out above 70°F. Confidence is moderately high given tight NWP agreement and a well-established June Gloom pattern; the key downside risk is a slower marine layer burn-off keeping the high in the 66-67°F range, while the upside risk of a quicker clearing could push toward 70°F.
